rounds.hypothesis: diagnose.json's invariant is right and complete: RLIMIT_FSIZE is never consulted on any write path, and the missing check belongs in InodeHandle's FileLike::write / write_at, which is the single funnel all five regular-file write syscalls reach. Mirroring generic_write_check_limits there (>= on the start offset, SIGXFSZ + EFBIG on the failing path, silent clamp to limit-offset otherwise) should make all 5 llseek01 assertions pass.
rounds.change: Added a private `check_fsize_limit(&self, offset, reader)` helper to kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs and called it from both `FileLike::write` (after the O_APPEND adjustment settles the offset, past the !is_offset_aware early return) and `FileLike::write_at` (likewise after its O_APPEND adjustment). The helper reads RLIMIT_FSIZE's soft limit from the current thread's process, returns Ok early on RLIM_INFINITY, enqueues SIGXFSZ and returns EFBIG when `offset >= limit`, and otherwise calls `reader.limit(limit - offset)` so the short write falls out of the existing `*offset += len` accounting. Made `RLIM_INFINITY` pub in kernel/src/process/rlimit.rs and re-exported it from kernel/src/process/mod.rs rather than hardcoding u64::MAX at the new call site. Uncommented `llseek01` in test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt. First cut gated only on `InodeType::is_regular_file()`.
rounds.outcome: green: `llseek01: pass (0.001s)`, kirk summary Passed: 5 / Failed: 0 / Broken: 0, matching the host baseline of 5/0/0 exactly (all five assertions now run, versus 1 before, since assertion 2 no longer trips tst_brk). `All conformance tests passed.` A 38-test write/rlimit regression sweep (write01-06, writev02/05/06, pwrite01-04, pwritev01, pwritev201, sendfile02-09, truncate02, ftruncate01/03, fallocate01/03, getrlimit01-03, setrlimit02-05, lseek01/07, llseek01-03) returned 132 passed / 0 failed, and a 38-test pipe/dup/open sweep returned 142 passed / 0 failed, confirming the SIGPIPE-adjacent pipe paths and the already-committed fsync03 behavior stay green.

rounds.hypothesis: Not a failure round -- a self-review round prompted by the phase's anti-overfitting check. `is_regular_file()` alone is too broad a scope for the invariant: procfs inodes report InodeType::File (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/procfs/template/file.rs:100-102), so /proc/[pid]/mem would be caught, and its write_at offsets are user-space *addresses* (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/procfs/pid/task/mem.rs:100-124, which forwards to vmar.write_alien). Under any finite RLIMIT_FSIZE a debugger writing to a tracee's memory above the limit would get a spurious EFBIG plus SIGXFSZ. The test never supplies this input, so green did not catch it.
rounds.change: Narrowed the predicate to `inode.type_().is_regular_file() && inode.page_cache().is_some()`, i.e. regular files whose bytes actually live in a page cache -- the same idiom `FileLike::mappable` already uses in this file to tell file-backed inodes from special ones. procfs and sysfs inodes take the `Inode::page_cache` default of `None` (kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs:407-409), so they are now exempt, while ramfs, ext2, exfat, virtiofs, overlayfs and memfd regular files all return `Some(_)` and remain covered. Also reordered the checks so the RLIM_INFINITY early return precedes the inode query, keeping the common unlimited case free of any inode work (this matters for overlayfs, whose page_cache() triggers a copy-up), and hoisted the zero-length short-circuit to the top so a zero-length write past the limit stays legal -- it cannot extend the file.
rounds.outcome: green: llseek01 re-run after the tightening still reports Passed: 5 / Failed: 0 and `All conformance tests passed.` A combined 45-test sweep (the write/rlimit set plus fsync02, pipe01, pipeio_1, pipeio_4, open01, openat01, dup01) returned 145 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` on aster-kernel are both clean.

layer: Matches diagnose.json's owning_layer: the per-open file-description layer inside the VFS, i.e. InodeHandle's FileLike::write and FileLike::write_at in kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs. This is the single funnel every regular-file write syscall reaches, it already holds the offset and applies the other per-open write policies (Rights::WRITE, O_APPEND), and it is above every concrete filesystem -- so the check sees a process's rlimits, which the filesystems below it have no business reading and which do not govern the internal metadata writes they also serve. The check is placed after the O_APPEND adjustment in both methods, so an append-only write is judged against the offset it will actually use rather than the stale one the caller passed.
generalizes: The fix covers all five write syscalls that share the defect, not just the sys_write that llseek01 walks: sys_write and do_sys_writev reach FileLike::write; sys_pwrite64, do_sys_pwritev and sys_sendfile (via FileHandle::write_bytes) reach FileLike::write_at. memfd writes route through the same funnel and are now bounded too. Nothing branches on llseek01's particular flag, size, or errno. The three inputs the test never supplies are handled deliberately: (a) a write starting strictly below the limit but ending past it is a silent short write clamped to limit-offset, not an error -- llseek01 only ever exercises the exactly-fitting case; (b) a zero-length write past the limit stays legal, since it cannot extend the file, which keeps the deliberate zero-length probe in do_sys_pwritev returning each file's own errno; (c) writes that cannot grow a file's contents are exempt -- pipes and sockets leave at the pre-existing !is_offset_aware early return, and devices plus pseudo-filesystem files are excluded by the page-cache predicate, which is what keeps /proc/[pid]/mem writes (whose offsets are user addresses, not file positions) from being rejected under a finite limit. The RLIM_INFINITY early return means the default configuration, where no process sets a limit, is unaffected: one relaxed atomic load and no inode work. Behavior with no current thread (kernel-mode unit tests) falls back to imposing no limit, following the existing Thread::current() fallbacks in ramfs and ext2. The two pre-existing enforcement sites in truncate.rs and fallocate.rs are untouched and remain correct for their own syscalls.
fix_summary: Adds RLIMIT_FSIZE enforcement to the regular-file write path, closing the gap named by the pre-existing FIXME at kernel/src/process/rlimit.rs:2. A new private `InodeHandle::check_fsize_limit` mirrors Linux's generic_write_check_limits: it compares the write's *starting* offset against the soft limit with `>=`, enqueues SIGXFSZ on the calling thread and returns EFBIG when the offset is at or beyond it, and otherwise clamps the transfer to `limit - offset`. It is designed against two Asterinas abstractions rather than transplanting Linux's structure. First, InodeHandle's FileLike::write / write_at pair is used as the equivalent of generic_write_checks -- Asterinas has no separate generic write-check entry point, but this pair is the single funnel all five regular-file write syscalls pass through, and its existing !is_offset_aware early returns already carve off the non-seekable files Linux exempts by other means. Second, the clamp is expressed as `VmReader::limit`, the tree's standard way to shorten a transfer (used the same way by memfd sealing and the block device layer), so the short write flows through the existing `*offset += len` accounting with no extra bookkeeping. Scoping uses `is_regular_file() && page_cache().is_some()`, the same predicate FileLike::mappable already uses here to separate file-backed inodes from special ones, because Asterinas gives procfs inodes InodeType::File and so type alone would wrongly capture /proc/[pid]/mem. RLIM_INFINITY was made pub and re-exported from the process module so the VFS can name it instead of hardcoding u64::MAX.
